articles.title: No Spin Zone? Lab Device Mimics Black Hole’s Energy-Sucking Power
articles.summary: Physicists built a stationary device that simulates extreme rotation, demonstrating the Penrose-Zel’dovich effect. Waves gained energy from the synthetic spin, confirming a 50-year-old theory. The breakthrough could advance wireless tech and quantum science.

articles.title: The Universe Is Too Big for Video Games — Here’s How Devs Fake It
articles.summary: Space’s true scale defies gaming: at a 1:10 billion scale, walking to the nearest star would cross the U.S. Developers compress distances and use visual tricks to balance realism and fun, while preserving a sense of cosmic awe.

articles.title: Deep-Sea Microbes Get a Pressure-Cooked Meal from Marine Snow
articles.summary: At depths of 2–6 km, hydrostatic pressure squeezes dissolved organic matter from marine snow, fueling microbial growth. Up to half the carbon leaks, challenging assumptions about carbon burial. The finding reshapes ocean carbon cycle models.
